title: Circular Hessenberg pairs and the tridiagonal relations
summary: A square matrix is said to be Hessenberg whenever each entry below the subdiagonal is zero, and each entry on the subdiagonal is nonzero. A Hessenberg matrix is called circular whenever the top-right corner entry is nonzero, and every other entry above the superdiagonal is zero. A circular Hessenberg pair consists of two diagonalizable linear maps on a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space, that each act on an eigenbasis of the other one in a circular Hessenberg fashion.
